paragraphs.text: A [red tea](red:definition) from Lincang. Its maker, Shangming Private Reserve Tea, labels it single-tree ancient wild red: leaf from one tree over 600 years old, fully oxidised, then finished by charcoal roasting, a [final drying](dian-hong:making) over heat that fixes the leaf once oxidation is done.

Lincang, in the south-west of Yunnan, holds Fengqing County, the home of [Dian Hong](dian-hong:definition), the red tea made from the province's large-leaf trees. Red tea from [old trees](dian-hong:old-tree-and-sun-dried) is a newer branch sold under the Yunnan red name. There is no agreed standard for it, and the trade has not settled whether it belongs to Dian Hong at all.

brewing.text: Dian Hong takes hot water, roughly 90 to 100°C. A common start is about 5 grams to 100 ml, with short steeps that lengthen slowly as the leaf opens.

notice.text: A full, sweet cup, often described as malty, with chocolate or cocoa and honey notes and sometimes something floral. The liquor runs golden to bright red, and a good grade has little bitterness.
